sections.html:
Columbia is the state capital and the county seat of Richland County. Some of its territory lies in Lexington and Kershaw counties, so confirm which county holds your parcel first. The answer tells you whose assessor and treasurer to call.

Columbia sits mid-state on the fall line, and the Broad and Saluda rivers merge here into the Congaree. A parcel near any of them should get a flood zone check. Columbia was laid out as a planned capital in 1786, and burned in part in 1865, so one street can hold a historic bungalow and the next a postwar ranch. Condition and price vary block by block, and a citywide average tells you little.

A Residential Rental Permit must be in hand before any tenant occupies a residential rental in the city. The rule covers units rented after July 1, 2016, and permits expire each year on December 31.

  • The nonbusiness form is for owners of up to 4 units, and the business form for owners of 5 or more.
  • Applications go to Code Enforcement at 920 Hemlock Drive, Columbia, SC 29201, and you pay online once approved.
  • For questions, call 803-545-4362.

Short-term rentals follow separate rules. An operator needs an STR Permit from Code Enforcement plus a Business License. Under Ordinance 2025-107, STRs are allowed in mixed-use, activity center and corridor, commercial and employment campus districts. In residential districts they are allowed on parcels fronting a four-lane arterial or collector street. An ordinance approved March 3, 2026 lets owner-occupied homes in residential districts operate without the four-lane condition. The city explains the rules on its STR page and the residential rentals page.

Selling with tenants in place? Renew the permit first. Any buyer or investor will want to see it, and a lapsed one is better fixed before you list.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
In this state the counties, not the cities, send and collect property tax bills. For a house inside Columbia, the value comes from the Richland County Assessor. You can pay from September 30 through January 15, and late charges build in stages after that (Code sections 12-45-70 and 12-45-180).

If still unpaid byAdded penalty
After January 153 percent
February 2Another 7 percent
March 17Another 5 percent

Your notice carries the exact amount and date, and the treasurer can confirm both. Should you sell partway through the year, the closing attorney usually settles what is owed out of your proceeds.

Disagree with your Richland County value? Put the objection in writing, either through the online portal or at the counter, and attach evidence for the figure you think is right. Time runs out 90 days after the date printed on the reassessment notice, or on the first penalty date of the current bill if that is sooner. You still owe the bill while the appeal is pending.

A representative filing on your behalf must hold a power of attorney on Form SC2848. When the owner is an LLC, include its organizing documents.

The Assessor's Office is at 2020 Hampton Street, Suite 2058, Columbia, SC 29204, phone 803-576-2640. The county's assessment appeal page has the online portal. A lower assessed value helps whoever owns the house next, yet it seldom moves today's sale price, so weigh the effort against your timeline.

sections.h2: What buyers notice about a Columbia house
sections.html:
Hot summers put air conditioning, attic ventilation and the roof under the inspector's spotlight in Columbia. Anything near the Broad, Saluda or Congaree rivers should come with a flood zone determination.

Describe a house near an interstate ramp or rail line candidly, because noise tends to come up at showings. Easy road access is still a plus for commuters, so mention both.

Columbia has many named neighborhoods, and each draws its own crowd. Arsenal Hill and Congaree Vista sit near downtown. Elmwood Park, the Waverly Historic District, Granby Mill Village and Rosewood are older, close-in areas. Five Points, Old Shandon and University Hill lie near the University of South Carolina, where rental demand shapes the market.

Investors tend to look near downtown and the campus, especially at houses with tenants already in place. A family buyer is more likely to want move-in condition, which is why a worn house in the same neighborhood can sit. Tell a cash buyer about any tenants, lease end dates and the rental permit status up front, since those details change what the house is worth to them.

sections.h2: Your options for a quick sale
sections.html:
Three routes are open to a Columbia seller: hire an agent, go it alone, or accept a cash offer. Houses near the university or downtown often draw investors. Houses that need work, or that have tenants in place, are harder to sell on the open market.

Here is how the paths differ in practice:

  • Agent listing suits a house in good shape when waiting out showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval is acceptable.
  • Selling yourself saves the commission but puts pricing, paperwork and negotiation on you.
  • A cash offer is normally as-is: no repair requests, no lender, and often a closing date of your choosing.

Collect four items before deciding: rental permit status, the county for your parcel, your latest tax bill and the payoff on your mortgage. Buyers and closing attorneys ask about all four.

sections.h2: What happens from offer to closing
sections.html:
Every sale moves through the same stages, but the clock differs. You accept a price and sign a purchase contract. The buyer then checks the property: inspection, title search and, if there is a loan, an appraisal. Cash buyers can often trim or drop the appraisal and lender stages, and those stages cause most of the slippage in a normal sale.

An attorney drafts the deed and settlement statement. At the table you sign, the attorney sends payoff money to your lender and clears any unpaid taxes from the proceeds, and the deed gets recorded. Whatever remains is yours.

Take a photo ID, your lender's name and loan number, keys and garage remotes, plus any leases and rental permit papers. A co-owner or heir named on the title must sign as well, so arrange that early. A lien or back taxes will not block a sale because they come out of the proceeds, but request payoff numbers well ahead of closing.

Little jobs help. Empty the rooms so inspectors can reach everything. Collect receipts for roof, HVAC or plumbing work to answer questions quickly. Keep utilities on in your name until closing day so the inspector can test the systems.

faqs.a: Mostly. Columbia is the Richland County seat, but parts of the city reach into Lexington and Kershaw counties. Confirm your parcel's county before you call an assessor or treasurer.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a rented house in Columbia?
faqs.a: The city requires a Residential Rental Permit for each rental unit, renewed every year by December 31. A buyer will want proof it is current. Code Enforcement can help at 803-545-4362.

faqs.q: When are Richland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due between September 30 and January 15. A 3 percent penalty starts after January 15. Ask the treasurer for the exact date and amount on your notice.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Columbia assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the dated reassessment notice, or until the first penalty date on the current bill if that comes first. An appeal does not stop the bill from coming due.

faqs.q: Can a buyer use a Columbia house as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Only where zoning and the city permit allow it. An STR Permit and a Business License are both required. In residential areas it depends on the street or on owner occupancy under the 2026 ordinance.
